blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Sum to \(n\) terms the series: \(1 + (a - b) + (a^{2} + ab + b^{2}) + (a^{3} + a^{2}b + ab^{2} + b^{3}) + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
Each bracket is a small G.P. in itself. (The second term is printed \((a - b)\); by the pattern and the answer key it is \((a + b)\), see the correction below.)
Plan: find the \(k\)th term as one fraction \( rac{a^{k} - b^{k}}{a - b}\), split the series into two G.P.s, sum each (assume \(a 
eq b\), \(a 
eq 1\), \(b 
eq 1\)).
steps:
Given: \(1 + (a + b) + (a^{2} + ab + b^{2}) + \cdots\) to \(n\) terms.
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Write the general term with the identity \(a^{k} - b^{k} = (a - b)(a^{k-1} + a^{k-2}b + \cdots + b^{k-1})\).

Find the \(k\)th term
\[T_k = a^{k-1} + a^{k-2}b + \cdots + b^{k-1}\]
\[= \dfrac{a^{k} - b^{k}}{a - b}\]
Why: In the \(k\)th bracket the power of \(a\) falls from \(k - 1\) to 0 while the power of \(b\) rises. For example \(a^{2} - b^{2} = (a - b)(a + b)\).

Check the formula on the first terms
\[T_1 = \dfrac{a - b}{a - b} = 1\]
\[T_2 = \dfrac{a^{2} - b^{2}}{a - b} = a + b\]
Why: The general term must give the actual terms of the series.

Add the \(n\) terms
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{a - b}\left[(a + a^{2} + \cdots + a^{n}) - (b + b^{2} + \cdots + b^{n})\right]\]
Why: Every term has the same denominator \(a - b\); collect the powers of \(a\) and of \(b\).

Sum each G.P.
\[a + \cdots + a^{n} = \dfrac{a(1 - a^{n})}{1 - a}\]
\[b + \cdots + b^{n} = \dfrac{b(1 - b^{n})}{1 - b}\]
Why: First term \(a\), ratio \(a\), \(n\) terms (and the same with \(b\)).

Put together as one fraction
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{a - b}\left[\dfrac{a(1 - a^{n})}{1 - a} - \dfrac{b(1 - b^{n})}{1 - b}\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{a(1 - b)(1 - a^{n}) - b(1 - a)(1 - b^{n})}{(a - b)(1 - a)(1 - b)}\]
Why: Common denominator \((1 - a)(1 - b)\).

Check: \(n = 2\)
\[\text{top} = a(1 - b)(1 - a^{2}) - b(1 - a)(1 - b^{2})\]
\[= (1 - a)(1 - b)(a - b)(1 + a + b)\]
Why: \(1 - a^{2} = (1 - a)(1 + a)\), \(1 - b^{2} = (1 - b)(1 + b)\), and \(a + a^{2} - b - b^{2} = (a - b)(1 + a + b)\). Dividing by the bottom leaves \(1 + (a + b)\), the sum of the first two terms.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the second term as \((a - b)\). By the pattern of the series (the \(k\)th term is \(a^{k-1} + a^{k-2}b + \cdots + b^{k-1}\)) and by the answer key, it should be \((a + b)\): the series is \(1 + (a + b) + (a^{2} + ab + b^{2}) + \cdots\). The working above uses \((a + b)\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Sum to \(n\) terms the series: \(r + (1 + k)r^{2} + (1 + k + k^{2})r^{3} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
The bracket in front of each power of \(r\) is a small G.P. in \(k\).
Plan: write the \(n\)th term as \( rac{1 - k^{n}}{1 - k}r^{n}\), split the series into two G.P.s (in \(r\) and in \(kr\)), and sum each (assume \(k 
eq 1\), \(r 
eq 1\), \(kr 
eq 1\)).
steps:
Given: \(r + (1 + k)r^{2} + (1 + k + k^{2})r^{3} + \cdots\) to \(n\) terms.
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Sum the bracket as a G.P. in \(k\), then split.

Find the \(n\)th term
\[T_n = (1 + k + \cdots + k^{n-1})r^{n}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 - k^{n}}{1 - k}\,r^{n}\]
Why: The bracket of the \(n\)th term has \(n\) terms: a G.P. with first term 1 and ratio \(k\).

Simplify the term
\[T_n = \dfrac{1}{1 - k}\left[r^{n} - (kr)^{n}\right]\]
Why: Multiply \(r^{n}\) into the top and use \(k^{n}r^{n} = (kr)^{n}\).

Add the \(n\) terms
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{1 - k}\left[(r + \cdots + r^{n}) - (kr + \cdots + (kr)^{n})\right]\]
Why: Each term has \(\frac{1}{1 - k}\) in front; collect the powers of \(r\) and of \(kr\).

Sum each G.P.
\[r + \cdots + r^{n} = \dfrac{r(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\]
\[kr + \cdots + (kr)^{n} = \dfrac{kr(1 - k^{n}r^{n})}{1 - kr}\]
Why: First G.P.: first term \(r\), ratio \(r\). Second: first term \(kr\), ratio \(kr\). Both have \(n\) terms.

Put the pieces together
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{1 - k}\left[\dfrac{r(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r} - \dfrac{kr(1 - k^{n}r^{n})}{1 - kr}\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{r}{1 - k}\left[\dfrac{1 - r^{n}}{1 - r} - \dfrac{k(1 - k^{n}r^{n})}{1 - kr}\right]\]
Why: Both fractions have \(r\) on top; take it outside.

Check: \(n = 1\)
\[\dfrac{r}{1 - k}\left[1 - k\right] = r\]
Why: For \(n = 1\): \(\frac{1 - r}{1 - r} = 1\) and \(\frac{k(1 - kr)}{1 - kr} = k\). The first term is \(r\).
